1. Create a Personal Budget Spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

Create a personal budget spreadsheet that tracks income, expenses, and savings over a specified period. Use formulas and functions to calculate totals, percentages, and remaining balances.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Personal Budget.

Step 3: Add the Spreadsheet Title

  1. In A1, type:
Personal Budget Tracker
  1. Select the range A1:F1.
  2. Click Merge & Center.
  3. Make the title Bold and increase the font size.

Step 4: Create the Income Table

Enter the following headings:

Cell Value
A3 Income Source
B3 Amount ()

Enter the sample data:

Income Source Amount ()
Salary 5000
Freelance 800
Other Income 200

Step 5: Calculate Total Income

In A8, type:

Total Income

In B8, enter:

=SUM(B4:B6)

Press Enter.

Step 6: Create the Expense Table

Starting from D3, enter:

Cell Value
D3 Expense Category
E3 Amount ()

Enter the sample expenses:

Expense Category Amount ()
Rent 1500
Food 700
Transport 250
Electricity 150
Internet 80
Entertainment 300

Step 7: Calculate Total Expenses

In D11, type:

Total Expenses

In E11, enter:

=SUM(E4:E9)

Step 8: Calculate Savings

In A10, type:

Savings

In B10, enter:

=B8-E11

Step 9: Calculate Expense Percentage

Create another column.

Cell Value
F3 % of Income

In F4, enter:

=E4/B8

Press Enter and copy the formula down to F9.

Format the cells as Percentage.

Step 10: Calculate Savings Percentage

In A12, type:

Savings %

In B12, enter:

=B10/B8

Format the cell as Percentage.

Step 11: Calculate Remaining Balance

In A14, type:

Remaining Balance

In B14, enter:

=B8-E11

Step 12: Apply Formatting

  • Make all headings Bold.
  • Apply All Borders to the tables.
  • Fill the header cells with a light background color.
  • Format the amount columns as Currency.
  • Format the percentage cells as Percentage.

Step 13: Apply Conditional Formatting

To highlight savings:

  1. Select B10.

  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting.

  3. Create a rule:

    • Green if the value is greater than 0.
    • Red if the value is less than 0.

Step 14: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Personal_Budget.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • SUM()
  • Basic arithmetic (-)
  • Division (/)

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Track income, expenses, and savings.
  • Calculate total income and total expenses automatically.
  • Calculate savings and remaining balance.
  • Display expense and savings percentages.
  • Highlight savings using conditional formatting.

2. Create a Sales Analysis Spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

A dataset containing sales data for a company is provided. Create a spreadsheet that calculates monthly sales totals, identifies the top-selling products, and visualizes sales trends using line charts or bar graphs. Use conditional formatting to highlight exceptional sales performances.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Sales Report.

Step 3: Create the Sales Dataset

Enter the following headers in Row 1:

Cell Value
A1 Month
B1 Product
C1 Sales ()

Enter the following sample data:

Month Product Sales ()
January Laptop 12000
January Mouse 2500
January Keyboard 3500
February Laptop 15000
February Mouse 2800
February Keyboard 4000
March Laptop 17000
March Mouse 3200
March Keyboard 4500
April Laptop 18000
April Mouse 3500
April Keyboard 5000

Step 4: Create the Monthly Sales Summary

Starting from E1, enter:

Cell Value
E1 Month
F1 Total Sales ()

Enter the months:

| E2 | January | | E3 | February | | E4 | March | | E5 | April |

Step 5: Calculate Monthly Sales Totals

In F2, enter the formula:

=SUMIF(A2:A13,E2,C2:C13)

Press Enter and drag the formula down to F5.

Step 6: Create the Product Sales Summary

Starting from H1, enter:

Cell Value
H1 Product
I1 Total Sales ()

Enter:

| H2 | Laptop | | H3 | Mouse | | H4 | Keyboard |

Step 7: Calculate Total Sales for Each Product

In I2, enter:

=SUMIF(B2:B13,H2,C2:C13)

Copy the formula down to I4.

Step 8: Identify the Top-Selling Product

In H6, type:

Top Selling Product

In I6, enter:

=INDEX(H2:H4,MATCH(MAX(I2:I4),I2:I4,0))

Step 9: Find the Highest Sales Amount

In H7, type:

Highest Sales

In I7, enter:

=MAX(I2:I4)

Step 10: Create a Line Chart for Monthly Sales

  1. Select the range E1:F5.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Line Chart.
  4. Select 2-D Line.
  5. Rename the chart Monthly Sales Trend.

Step 11: Create a Bar Chart for Product Sales

  1. Select the range H1:I4.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Column Chart.
  4. Choose Clustered Column.
  5. Rename the chart Product Sales Comparison.

Step 12: Apply Conditional Formatting

To highlight exceptional sales:

  1. Select C2:C13.
  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Greater Than.
  3. Enter 15000.
  4. Choose Green Fill with Dark Green Text.
  5. Click OK.

Sales values greater than 15,000 will be highlighted automatically.

Step 13: Calculate Overall Sales

In E7, type:

Overall Sales

In F7, enter:

=SUM(C2:C13)

Step 14: Calculate Average Sales

In E8, type:

Average Sales

In F8, enter:

=AVERAGE(C2:C13)

Step 15: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Sales_Report.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • SUM()
  • SUMIF()
  • MAX()
  • INDEX()
  • MATCH()
  • AVERAGE()

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store and organize sales data.
  • Calculate monthly sales totals automatically.
  • Identify the top-selling product.
  • Display sales trends using line and bar charts.
  • Highlight exceptional sales using conditional formatting.
  • Calculate the overall and average sales automatically.

3. Design a Grade Book Spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

Design a grade book spreadsheet that calculates students' final grades based on assignments, exams, and participation. Incorporate a weighted grading system, use formulas to calculate averages and final grades, apply conditional formatting to indicate performance levels, and generate reports to track individual student progress.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Grade Book.

Step 3: Create the Student Grade Table

Enter the following headings in Row 1:

Cell Value
A1 Student Name
B1 Assignment (%)
C1 Exam (%)
D1 Participation (%)
E1 Final Grade (%)
F1 Grade
G1 Status

Step 4: Enter Sample Student Data

Student Name Assignment Exam Participation
Alice 85 90 95
Bob 78 72 80
Charlie 92 88 90
David 65 70 75
Emma 98 95 100

Step 5: Apply the Weighted Grading System

Use the following weight distribution:

  • Assignments: 40%
  • Exams: 50%
  • Participation: 10%

In E2, enter:

=(B2*40%)+(C2*50%)+(D2*10%)

Press Enter and drag the formula down to the remaining students.

Step 6: Assign Letter Grades

In F2, enter:

=IF(E2>=90,"A",IF(E2>=80,"B",IF(E2>=70,"C",IF(E2>=60,"D","F"))))

Copy the formula down to all students.

Step 7: Determine Pass or Fail Status

In G2, enter:

=IF(E2>=40,"Pass","Fail")

Copy the formula down.

Step 8: Calculate the Class Average

In D9, type:

Class Average

In E9, enter:

=AVERAGE(E2:E6)

Step 9: Find the Highest Grade

In D10, type:

Highest Grade

In E10, enter:

=MAX(E2:E6)

Step 10: Find the Lowest Grade

In D11, type:

Lowest Grade

In E11, enter:

=MIN(E2:E6)

Step 11: Count the Number of Students

In D12, type:

Total Students

In E12, enter:

=COUNTA(A2:A6)

Step 12: Apply Conditional Formatting

Highlight student performance levels.

  1. Select E2:E6.
  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting.

Create the following rules:

  • Green Fill for grades 90 and above.
  • Yellow Fill for grades 70 to 89.
  • Red Fill for grades below 70.

Step 13: Generate a Student Progress Report

Create a summary table starting from I1.

Cell Value
I1 Student Name
J1 Final Grade (%)
K1 Grade
L1 Status

Copy the data from columns A, E, F, and G into the report.

This report provides a quick overview of each student's academic performance.

Step 14: Create a Bar Chart

  1. Select A1:A6 and E1:E6.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Choose Column Chart → Clustered Column.
  4. Rename the chart Student Final Grades.

Step 15: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Grade_Book.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • AVERAGE()
  • MAX()
  • MIN()
  • COUNTA()
  • IF()

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store student marks for assignments, exams, and participation.
  • Calculate weighted final grades automatically.
  • Assign letter grades.
  • Display pass/fail status.
  • Calculate class average, highest grade, lowest grade, and total number of students.
  • Highlight performance levels using conditional formatting.
  • Generate a student progress report.
  • Visualize student performance using a bar chart.

4. Create an Inventory Management Spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

Create a spreadsheet that tracks inventory for a hypothetical business. Include columns for item names, quantities, unit prices, and total values. Use formulas to automatically update inventory totals, generate alerts for low stock, and create visualizations to represent inventory levels over time.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Inventory Management.

Step 3: Create the Inventory Table

Enter the following headings in Row 1:

Cell Value
A1 Item Name
B1 Quantity
C1 Unit Price ()
D1 Total Value ()
E1 Stock Status

Step 4: Enter Sample Inventory Data

Item Name Quantity Unit Price ()
Laptop 20 800
Mouse 60 20
Keyboard 40 35
Monitor 15 180
Printer 8 250

Step 5: Calculate Total Value for Each Item

In D2, enter:

=B2*C2

Press Enter and drag the formula down to D6.

Step 6: Generate Low Stock Alerts

Assume that stock below 10 units is considered low.

In E2, enter:

=IF(B2<10,"Low Stock","In Stock")

Press Enter and drag the formula down to E6.

Step 7: Calculate Total Inventory Value

In C8, type:

Total Inventory Value

In D8, enter:

=SUM(D2:D6)

Step 8: Calculate Total Quantity in Stock

In C9, type:

Total Quantity

In D9, enter:

=SUM(B2:B6)

Step 9: Find the Highest Priced Item

In C10, type:

Highest Unit Price

In D10, enter:

=MAX(C2:C6)

Step 10: Find the Average Unit Price

In C11, type:

Average Unit Price

In D11, enter:

=AVERAGE(C2:C6)

Step 11: Apply Conditional Formatting

To highlight low stock items:

  1. Select B2:B6.
  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than.
  3. Enter 10.
  4. Choose Red Fill with Dark Red Text.
  5. Click OK.

Items with fewer than 10 units will be highlighted automatically.

Step 12: Create a Bar Chart for Inventory Levels

  1. Select the range A1:B6.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Column Chart.
  4. Choose Clustered Column.
  5. Rename the chart Current Inventory Levels.

Step 13: Create an Inventory Tracking Table

Starting from G1, create the following table to record inventory levels over time.

Date Laptop Mouse Keyboard Monitor Printer
Week 1 20 60 40 15 8
Week 2 18 58 38 14 7
Week 3 16 55 36 12 6
Week 4 15 52 35 10 5

Step 14: Create a Line Chart for Inventory Trends

  1. Select the tracking table created in Step 13.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Line Chart.
  4. Choose 2-D Line.
  5. Rename the chart Inventory Levels Over Time.

Step 15: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Inventory_Management.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • SUM()
  • AVERAGE()
  • MAX()
  • IF()

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store inventory details for all items.
  • Calculate the total value of each inventory item automatically.
  • Calculate the total inventory quantity and overall inventory value.
  • Generate automatic low stock alerts.
  • Highlight low stock items using conditional formatting.
  • Display current inventory levels using a bar chart.
  • Track inventory changes over time using a line chart.

5. Create a Loan Repayment Calculator in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

Loan parameters, such as principal amount, interest rate, and loan term, are provided. Create a spreadsheet that calculates monthly loan payments, remaining balances, and interest paid over time using appropriate formulas. Create a chart to visualize the loan's repayment schedule.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Loan Calculator.

Step 3: Enter the Loan Parameters

Create the following table:

Cell Value
A2 Principal Amount ()
B2 100000
A3 Annual Interest Rate
B3 8%
A4 Loan Term (Years)
B4 5

Step 4: Calculate the Monthly Loan Payment

In A6, type:

Monthly Payment

In B6, enter:

=PMT(B3/12,B4*12,-B2)

Press Enter.

Step 5: Create the Loan Repayment Schedule

Enter the following headings starting from A9:

Cell Value
A9 Month
B9 Monthly Payment
C9 Interest Paid
D9 Principal Paid
E9 Remaining Balance

Step 6: Enter the First Month

In A10, enter:

1

In B10, enter:

=B6

In C10, enter:

=B2*(B3/12)

In D10, enter:

=B10-C10

In E10, enter:

=B2-D10

Step 7: Complete the Remaining Months

In A11, enter:

=A10+1

Drag down until the final month (60 for a 5-year loan).

In B11, enter:

=B6

Copy down.

In C11, enter:

=E10*(B3/12)

Copy down.

In D11, enter:

=B11-C11

Copy down.

In E11, enter:

=E10-D11

Copy down until the loan balance reaches approximately 0.

Step 8: Calculate Total Interest Paid

In G2, type:

Total Interest Paid

In H2, enter:

=SUM(C10:C69)

Step 9: Calculate Total Amount Paid

In G3, type:

Total Amount Paid

In H3, enter:

=SUM(B10:B69)

Step 10: Apply Conditional Formatting

Highlight the remaining balance.

  1. Select E10:E69.

  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting.

  3. Create a rule:

    • Green fill when the value equals 0.
    • Yellow fill for values greater than 0.

Step 11: Create a Line Chart for the Repayment Schedule

  1. Select the columns Month and Remaining Balance (A9:A69 and E9:E69).
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Line Chart.
  4. Choose 2-D Line.
  5. Rename the chart Loan Repayment Schedule.

Step 12: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Loan_Repayment_Calculator.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • PMT()
  • SUM()
  • Basic arithmetic (+, -, *, /)

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store the loan principal, interest rate, and loan term.
  • Calculate the monthly loan payment automatically.
  • Calculate the monthly interest and principal payments.
  • Display the remaining loan balance after each payment.
  • Calculate the total interest paid and total amount repaid.
  • Highlight the completed loan balance using conditional formatting.
  • Visualize the repayment schedule with a line chart.

6. Perform Data Analysis Using Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

A dataset is provided for analysis. Create a spreadsheet to calculate summary statistics, sort and filter the data, and generate charts or graphs to visualize patterns or trends within the dataset.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Data Analysis.

Step 3: Create the Dataset

Enter the following headings in Row 1:

Cell Value
A1 Employee
B1 Department
C1 Age
D1 Salary ()

Enter the sample data:

Employee Department Age Salary ()
John HR 28 42000
Alice IT 30 55000
Bob Sales 35 48000
Emma IT 27 60000
David HR 40 50000
Sophia Sales 32 53000

Step 4: Calculate Summary Statistics

Create the following summary table:

Cell Value
F2 Average Salary
F3 Highest Salary
F4 Lowest Salary
F5 Total Salary
F6 Number of Employees

Step 5: Enter the Formulas

In G2, enter:

=AVERAGE(D2:D7)

In G3, enter:

=MAX(D2:D7)

In G4, enter:

=MIN(D2:D7)

In G5, enter:

=SUM(D2:D7)

In G6, enter:

=COUNTA(A2:A7)

Step 6: Sort the Data

  1. Select the dataset (A1:D7).
  2. Go to the Data tab.
  3. Click Sort.
  4. Sort by Salary ().
  5. Choose Largest to Smallest.
  6. Click OK.

Step 7: Filter the Data

  1. Select the dataset (A1:D7).
  2. Go to the Data tab.
  3. Click Filter.
  4. Click the filter arrow in the Department column.
  5. Select a department (e.g., IT) to display only employees from that department.

Step 8: Apply Conditional Formatting

Highlight employees with high salaries.

  1. Select D2:D7.
  2. Go to Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Greater Than.
  3. Enter:
50000
  1. Choose Green Fill with Dark Green Text.
  2. Click OK.

Step 9: Create a Bar Chart

  1. Select the Employee and Salary columns (A1:A7 and D1:D7).
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Column Chart.
  4. Choose Clustered Column.
  5. Rename the chart Employee Salary Comparison.

Step 10: Create a Pie Chart

  1. Select the Department and Salary columns.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Pie Chart.
  4. Choose 2-D Pie.
  5. Rename the chart Salary Distribution by Department.

Step 11: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Data_Analysis_Report.xlsx.

Excel Functions Used

  • AVERAGE()
  • MAX()
  • MIN()
  • SUM()
  • COUNTA()

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store and organize the dataset.
  • Calculate summary statistics such as average, maximum, minimum, total, and employee count.
  • Sort the data based on salary.
  • Filter the data by department.
  • Highlight high salaries using conditional formatting.
  • Visualize the data using bar and pie charts to identify patterns and trends.

7. Create Time Series Charts in Microsoft Excel

Problem Statement

Select a dataset (e.g., stock prices, weather data, population growth, etc.) and create line charts or area charts to visualize trends over time. Choose appropriate chart types, label the axes, and add chart titles and legends to make the visualization clear and informative.

Step 1: Open Microsoft Excel

  • Open Microsoft Excel.
  • Click Blank Workbook.

Step 2: Rename the Worksheet

  • Rename Sheet1 to Time Series Analysis.

Step 3: Create the Dataset

Enter the following headings in Row 1:

Cell Value
A1 Month
B1 Average Temperature (°C)

Enter the sample data:

Month Average Temperature (°C)
January 18
February 20
March 25
April 30
May 34
June 33
July 31
August 30
September 29
October 27
November 23
December 19

Step 4: Create a Line Chart

  1. Select the range A1:B13.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Line Chart.
  4. Choose 2-D Line.

Step 5: Add a Chart Title

  1. Click the chart title.
  2. Rename it to:
Monthly Average Temperature Trend

Step 6: Add Axis Titles

  1. Click the chart.
  2. Go to Chart Design → Add Chart Element → Axis Titles.
  3. Add the following:
  • Horizontal Axis: Month
  • Vertical Axis: Temperature (°C)

Step 7: Display the Legend

  1. Click the chart.
  2. Go to Chart Design → Add Chart Element → Legend.
  3. Choose Right (or any preferred position).

Step 8: Create an Area Chart

  1. Select the range A1:B13.
  2. Go to the Insert tab.
  3. Click Area Chart.
  4. Choose 2-D Area.
  5. Rename the chart Monthly Temperature Analysis.

Step 9: Format the Charts

  • Increase the chart title font size.
  • Apply a suitable chart style.
  • Resize the charts for better readability.
  • Ensure the axis labels and legend are clearly visible.

Step 10: Save the Workbook

  • Click File → Save As.
  • Save the workbook as Time_Series_Charts.xlsx.

Excel Features Used

  • Line Chart
  • Area Chart
  • Chart Title
  • Axis Titles
  • Legend

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store time-series data in a structured format.
  • Visualize trends using a line chart and an area chart.
  • Display properly labeled axes.
  • Include informative chart titles and legends.
  • Present the data clearly for trend analysis over time.

Excel Functions Used

  • SUM()
  • AVERAGE()

Outcome

The completed spreadsheet will:

  • Store monthly sales data for multiple products.
  • Calculate total and average sales automatically.
  • Compare sales trends using a combo chart with columns and a line.
  • Display chart titles, axis titles, legends, and data labels.
  • Highlight high sales values using conditional formatting.
  • Help identify relationships and trends between the different product sales over time.

Formula Reference

1. Mathematical & Statistical Functions

Function Syntax What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
SUM() =SUM(range) Adds all numbers in a range. =SUM(B4:B6) adds up all income sources. Budget, Sales, Inventory, Loan, Data Analysis, Product Comparison
AVERAGE() =AVERAGE(range) Calculates the arithmetic mean of a range. =AVERAGE(E2:E6) calculates the class average grade. Grade Book, Data Analysis, Product Comparison, Combo Chart
MAX() =MAX(range) Returns the largest number in a range. =MAX(I2:I4) finds the highest product sales total. Sales Analysis, Grade Book, Inventory, Data Analysis, Product Comparison
MIN() =MIN(range) Returns the smallest number in a range. =MIN(E2:E6) finds the lowest final grade. Grade Book, Data Analysis
COUNTA() =COUNTA(range) Counts the number of non-empty cells in a range (useful for counting entries). =COUNTA(A2:A6) counts how many students are listed. Grade Book, Data Analysis

2. Logical Functions (Conditional)

Function Syntax What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
IF() =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false) Checks a condition and returns one value if true, another if false. =IF(E2>=90,"A",IF(E2>=80,"B","C")) assigns letter grades. Grade Book, Inventory Management

3. Conditional Aggregation (Lookup & Sum with Criteria)

Function Syntax What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
SUMIF() =SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range) Adds values in a range only if they meet a given condition. =SUMIF(A2:A13, E2, C2:C13) adds sales only for the month in E2. Sales Analysis

4. Lookup & Reference Functions (Advanced)

Function Syntax What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
INDEX() =INDEX(array, row_num, [column_num]) Returns a value from a specific position within a table/range. =INDEX(H2:H4, ...) returns the product name from the list. Sales Analysis
MATCH() =MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array, [match_type]) Finds the position of a value in a list. =MATCH(MAX(I2:I4), I2:I4, 0) finds which row has the max sales. Sales Analysis
INDEX + MATCH (Combo) Combined together Looks up a value dynamically (more flexible than VLOOKUP). =INDEX(H2:H4, MATCH(MAX(I2:I4), I2:I4, 0)) identifies the top-selling product. Sales Analysis

5. Financial Functions

Function Syntax What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
PMT() =PMT(rate, nper, pv, [fv], [type]) Calculates the periodic payment for a loan based on constant payments and a constant interest rate. =PMT(B3/12, B4*12, -B2) calculates the monthly loan payment. Loan Repayment Calculator

6. Arithmetic Operators (Basic Building Blocks)

Operator What It Does Example from the Tutorials Used In
+ (Plus) Addition =(B2*40%)+(C2*50%)+(D2*10%) adds weighted scores together. Grade Book, Loan Calculator
- (Minus) Subtraction =B8-E11 subtracts total expenses from total income to get savings. Budget, Loan Calculator
* (Asterisk) Multiplication =B2*C2 multiplies quantity by unit price to get total value. Inventory, Grade Book (for weights)
/ (Forward slash) Division =E4/B8 divides an expense by total income to get a percentage. Budget, Loan Calculator
% (Percent) Percentage =B2*40% applies a 40% weight to an assignment score. Grade Book
